title: The supplied evidence does not fully establish comparability of the baseline and relative-position runs
central_question: Were each absolute-position baseline and its corresponding relative-position model trained, selected, decoded, and evaluated under matched conditions so that the reported BLEU differences can be attributed to the position representations?
observed_facts: The authors state that they generated baseline results to isolate the impact of relative position representations from other changes to the library and experimental configuration. The reported model settings nevertheless differ between base and big configurations: the base model is trained for 100,000 steps without checkpoint averaging on K40 GPUs, whereas the big model is trained for 300,000 steps with the last 20 checkpoints averaged on P100 GPUs. The supplied units do not give complete, separate baseline training and checkpoint-selection details.

The authors state that they generated sinusoidal-position baseline results to isolate relative position representations from changes to the underlying library and experimental configuration. title: The measured efficiency evidence is narrower than the broad implementation claim

observed_facts: The authors describe an efficient tensor-reshaping implementation and report a 7% decrease in training steps per second while retaining the same model and batch sizes on P100 GPUs as Vaswani et al. They also give asymptotic storage-complexity expressions for relative-position representations.

The authors describe a tensor-reshaping implementation for the relative-position terms and state that the same approach applies to the output computation. For the machine translation experiments, they report a 7% decrease in steps per second while retaining the same model and batch sizes on P100 GPUs as Vaswani et al. (2017). They also state asymptotic storage changes from O(bhndz) to O(bhndz + n²da), with relative representations shared across heads and sequences.

title: The stated overall storage bound may describe only selected attention tensors
central_question: Check the original Section 3.3 layout and surrounding text for an explicit restriction of the space analysis to representation storage.
observed_facts: The implementation passage calls O(bhndz) the baseline overall self-attention space complexity and O(bhndz + n²da) the complexity with relative representations shared across heads and sequences. Nearby text describes computing compatibility values for all pairs of positions through n-by-dz and dz-by-n matrix products. The experimental setup also distinguishes base models with unique representations per layer and head from big models with unique representations per layer.
suspected_problem: The word 'overall' may leave unclear whether the bound includes the pairwise attention scores and normalized weights, or only projected input and relative-representation tensors. In an implementation that materializes attention matrices, their O(bhn²) storage would also need accounting. The stated shared-head bound also needs to be distinguished from the base experiment's unshared-head configuration.
scientific_significance: The tensor scope and sharing assumptions determine how memory scales with sequence length, batch size, and head count. An ambiguous bound could lead readers to underestimate memory requirements or apply the shared-head estimate to the base model when reproducing the method.
verification_questions: Check the original Section 3.3 layout and surrounding text for an explicit restriction of the space analysis to representation storage.
Which tensors are retained during forward computation and training, and are the pairwise score and weight tensors materialized?
How does the memory accounting change for the base model's unique representations per head?
Does the implementation avoid broadcasting while still retaining an O(bhn²) attention tensor, and is this distinction documented?
source_limitations: The concern is based on the supplied prose complexity statement, not an independently verified implementation memory trace.
Omitted text and unverified technical objects may clarify the intended scope.
The reported ability to preserve model and batch sizes on P100 GPUs provides practical counterevidence to a severe memory limitation, but does not by itself define the asymptotic accounting.
impact_rationale: Original candidates agree; severity remains unverified
consolidation_rationale: This candidate questions the tensor scope and sharing assumptions of the stated asymptotic storage bound. Although related to practical efficiency, resolving the theoretical accounting requires a distinct check of which tensors the bound includes and how head sharing changes it.

title: The claim about generalization to unseen sequence lengths is presented without a corresponding evaluation in the supplied evidence
central_question: Does the claim that clipping enables generalization to unseen sequence lengths refer to representations remaining defined or to maintained predictive performance, and does the complete paper provide training-length limits and evaluation outside those limits to support the latter interpretation?
observed_facts: The authors state that relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length and that clipping the maximum distance enables generalization to sequence lengths not seen during training. The supplied experiments vary the clipping distance on the WMT English-to-German newstest2013 development set, but the reported setup does not state that training and evaluation use deliberately different sequence-length ranges.

The authors state that their relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length and that clipping enables generalization to sequence lengths unseen during training. The supplied model-variation experiments instead vary the clipping distance in a base English-to-German model evaluated on newstest2013. Their discussion also notes that multiple encoder layers may propagate precise relative position information beyond the clipping distance.

The authors state that clipping relative distances enables generalization to sequence lengths not seen during training. The reported clipping experiment varies k on the WMT English-to-German newstest2013 development set, while the supplied experimental setup does not describe an evaluation in which test sequence lengths are deliberately outside the training range.

The background states that the relative position representations are invariant to total sequence length and associates this property with generalization to lengths unseen during training. The conclusion that clipping enables this property may therefore rely on architectural reasoning rather than a dedicated empirical control. / The wording may blur two distinct properties: being able to assign a learned relation representation to every pair at a new sequence length, and maintaining translation quality when evaluating beyond training lengths.
